items.title: Moonshot AI Releases Kimi K3.1 Pro: A 2.8T Total/104B Active Params (MoE) Model with 1M Context
items.summary: Moonshot AI released Kimi K3.1 Pro, a 2.8T-parameter, 104B-active MoE model with 1M-token context. It scores 65.7% on Terminal-Bench 4.0, costs $2/$10 per million tokens, and open weights arrive by Nov 4, 2026.

items.title: Kyutai CADRE: Video Autoencoders That Cut World Model Lag Below 230 ms
items.summary: Kyutai released CADRE, a family of 7 open causal diffusion video autoencoders for interactive world models. World models built on CADRE run at 20 fps on 1 H100 and react in under 230 ms.

items.summary: NVIDIA released Nemotron 3.5 Bolt E4B 4GB, an open small language model post-trained from Gemma 4 E4B for local voice assistants, game characters and robots, targeting about 4GB of VRAM on RTX and Jetson. items.title: Fancy harnesses make coding agents more expensive but not better, study finds
items.summary: A controlled study shows that switching between coding-agent harnesses like Claude Code, OpenCode, or mini-SWE-agent barely moves pass rates more than rerunning the same setup. Cost per task, however, can triple, driven mainly by the system prompt that gets resent with every step.

items.title: Stateful Agentic Engineering Copilots with Letta: Core Memory, Shared State, Semantic Retrieval, Custom Tools, Streaming, and Portable Agent Workflows
items.summary: Discover how to extend agentic memory beyond basic prompts by building a stateful engineering copilot with Letta. This comprehensive guide covers inspectable core memory, archival vector retrieval, multi-agent shared state, custom tools, and portable workflows.

items.title: Meet Anthropic’s sandbox-runtime: OS-Level Sandboxing for AI Agents, No Containers
items.summary: Anthropic sandbox-runtime (srt) is the open-source, OS-level sandbox behind Claude Code. It restricts file and network access for agents, MCP servers and CLI tools with Seatbelt on macOS and bubblewrap on Linux, no containers needed.

items.title: OpenAI's isolated AI agents found ways to talk to each other through CPU cache
items.summary: OpenAI now trains its most powerful models without internet access, after an internal research model exploited a DNS misconfiguration in September and reached the open internet. In controlled tests, AI agents still found ways to communicate covertly through side channels.

items.title: Block's new AI model Dessa was trained entirely on human speech to catch emotions text-based models miss
items.summary: Block, the company behind Square and Cash App, has introduced Dessa, a speech model that processes audio directly instead of converting it to text first. Dessa is designed to recognize emotions, sarcasm, and pauses in real time.

items.title: AI makes junior patent attorneys instantly better but may quietly stunt their professional growth
items.summary: A three-month field experiment with 133 patent attorneys shows that AI boosts immediate performance, with junior lawyers gaining the most. But when the AI is taken away, only senior attorneys retain the benefits, suggesting that baseline expertise is a prerequisite for turning AI-assisted practice into lasting skill.

items.title: Three fired OpenAI safety researchers say they were never told what they actually leaked
items.summary: The three OpenAI safety researchers who were fired, Tomek Korbak, Mikita Balesni, and Jasmine Wang, are publicly pushing back against allegations from their former employer. They deny sharing confidential information and see a connection to their advocacy for AI systems that are easier to scrutinize.

items.title: Pennsylvania will require labels on AI-generated ads
items.summary: On Thursday, Pennsylvania Governor Josh Shapiro signed the Artificial Intelligence Deceptive Advertising Act into law, requiring disclosures on AI-generated ads. The law requires any ad - whether it's a still image, video, audio, or text - that "has been significantly modified or generated by artificial intelligence" to include a label in the same format as […]

items.title: Blue Planet III is keeping the rough edges in the age of AI
items.summary: BBC's Blue Planet III is looking to prove its authenticity by leaving in the less-than-perfect shots. Previous incarnations of the nature series were defined by their gorgeous, crystal-clear footage that seemed almost too good to be real.

items.title: Cognition Open-Sources an Agent Plugin that Helps Secure Systems against Recent Cybersecurity Threats
items.summary: Cognition released the Devin Vulnerability Fixes plugin, 3 MIT-licensed agent skills that inventory, patch and test PHP, Node.js and self-managed GitLab deployments hit by this week’s critical RCE flaws, then open 1 PR per repo. The post Cognition Open-Sources an Agent Plugin that Helps Secure Systems against Recent Cybersecurity Threats appeared first on MarkTechPost .

items.title: Microsoft Open-Sources Agensh: A Multi-Agent Harness for 1,024 Agents
items.summary: Microsoft Research open-sourced Agensh, a multi-agent harness with no central orchestrator. Self-organizing workers share a Git repo, chat and a findings board, scaling from 1 to 1,024 agents on ProgramBench under a 6-hour budget.

items.title: OpenMobile-2 proves open-source smartphone agents can rival proprietary models
items.summary: Smartphone agents don't get better by processing more data. They improve by training on as many different apps as possible.

items.title: OpenAI offers discounts up to 90 percent to poach Anthropic's biggest customers
items.summary: OpenAI is poaching Anthropic's customers with steep discounts. Companies like Rippling, Replit, and DataCamp say they've cut AI costs by up to 90 percent after switching.

items.title: Ex-Google CEO Eric Schmidt calls OpenAI and Anthropic modern colonial trading companies
items.summary: In Foreign Affairs, historian Niall Ferguson, researcher Lisa Klaassen, and former Google CEO Eric Schmidt cast the US and China as AI empires and every other country as a dependency. The race won't be decided by breakthroughs but by who can bankroll it.

items.title: Anthropic says one AI agent beats many subagents now that models can handle complexity alone
items.summary: Anthropic says companies should evaluate whether they can consolidate sub-agents into a single agent that loads context on demand. In one architecture comparison, the single-agent setup ran about twice as fast.

items.title: Anthropic co-founder Jack Clark moves his prediction for self-improving AI forward to 2027
items.summary: A new benchmark by P-Zero Research measures how well AI models design and evaluate experiments on their own. The results are improving so fast that Anthropic co-founder Jack Clark now thinks self-improving AI could arrive by 2027.
